questions.q: What is the PEEL structure and why is it used in writing analytical answers for literature?
questions.a: PEEL stands for Point, Evidence, Explanation, Link. It is used to structure analytical paragraphs so that each claim is supported by textual evidence and connected to the broader theme. A wrong answer (e.g., "PEEL is a fruit" or "It means writing a summary") reveals the student does not know the standard answer-writing framework for CBSE literature questions.

questions.q: In a character sketch of Crocker-Harris, a student writes: "Crocker-Harris is a very strict teacher who follows rules. He is not liked by students. Taplow dislikes him." What is missing from this answer?
questions.a: The answer lacks textual evidence (quotes or specific incidents), explanation of how the evidence shows the trait, and a link to the play's themes (e.g., the gap between duty and humanity). A wrong answer that only lists missing elements without explaining why they matter shows the student cannot evaluate answer quality.

questions.q: Rewrite the following weak diary entry by Taplow into a strong one using PEEL. Weak entry: "Today I met Mr. Crocker-Harris. He gave me extra work. I am sad. I also met Frank. He is nice." (Write the improved version.)
questions.a: A strong version would include: Point (Taplow's resentment), Evidence (specific dialogue: "I'm here because I want my remove"), Explanation (shows his frustration with unfairness), Link (reflects the theme of student-teacher power dynamics). A poor rewrite that just adds adjectives without structural change reveals inability to apply PEEL.

questions.q: Compare the teacher-student relationship in "The Browning Version" with that in "The Portrait of a Lady" (Class 11). What common theme emerges, and how do the texts differ in portraying it?
questions.a: Both show a relationship built on respect and duty, but "The Browning Version" portrays a formal, emotionally distant dynamic (Crocker-Harris/Taplow) while "The Portrait of a Lady" shows a warm, evolving bond (grandmother/granddaughter). A wrong answer that only lists similarities without contrasting narrative techniques (play vs. prose) shows lack of analytical depth.

questions.q: Evaluate this claim: "Writing a formal letter from Taplow to the headmaster complaining about Crocker-Harris would be an appropriate writing task for this chapter." Justify your evaluation.
questions.a: Inappropriate. Taplow respects Crocker-Harris despite fear; he would not complain. A formal letter task should align with character motivation. A wrong answer that says "yes, because it's a formal letter practice" reveals the student prioritizes format over character consistency and textual integrity.

questions.q: Create a 4-line dialogue between Frank and Taplow after the play ends, where Taplow reflects on Crocker-Harris's farewell speech. Use stage directions.
questions.a: A good response includes: stage directions in brackets, character names, dialogue that reflects Taplow's changed perception (e.g., "He isn't a monster, Frank. He's just... human"), and Frank's supportive tone. A poor response that writes a narrative paragraph instead of dialogue format shows misunderstanding of dramatic writing conventions.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Writing Skills based on the chapter "The Browning Version" refers to the ability to compose structured, evidence-based responses (such as character sketches, thematic analyses, dialogue rewrites, formal letters, and diary entries) that demonstrate ______ of the play's themes, characters, and dramatic techniques, using appropriate register, format, and textual evidence as per CBSE Class 11 examination requirements.
Fill in the blank: Imagine you're asked to write a ______ sketch of Crocker-Harris for your exam.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student can independently write a 150-200 word analytical response (e.g., character sketch of Taplow or Crocker-Harris, thematic paragraph on teacher-student relationship, or a formal letter from Taplow's perspective) using the PEEL structure, embedding at least two textual references, and maintaining formal tone and correct format.
